title: Asymptotic Descent: every sufficiently large start has a finite descent certificate
statement: There exists N such that every n >= N admits a realized finite itinerary w with J^{|w|}(n) < n (equivalently: no AboveAnchor prefix of the orbit of n extends indefinitely). Together with a finite check of the starts below N, strict integer descent and strong induction would give arrival at 1; this is exactly the missing induction hypothesis of Paper A Section 6. The Lean-verified constraint on the negation (J-above-anchor-hug-domination): a descent-free flight keeps the exponent walk u_k = a_k log2 3 - k nonnegative and dominates the exact hug itinerary in odd count at every prefix, so its odd-letter density is at least log 2 / log 3 in every prefix.
tested_range: descent-time census [2, 2000000]: every start descends below itself (max D = 257 at n = 1122603; the six high-flyers 48443/275485/412027/463157/1245741/1267909 resolve in the exact gmpy2 retry pass with peaks up to 6.5e6 bits); see data/research/juggler/above_anchor_walk/summary.json
notes: Weaker than the full Juggler conjecture (finitely many small starts remain) and stronger than the certified-density results (13/16 proved, Paper B): it is pointwise for large n, not density. The walk-envelope route to proving it requires floor-defect lower bounds at walk near-minima; the Phase-0 census finds first descents are overwhelmingly gap descents (the parity itinerary itself goes exponent-negative), so the binding mechanism is the parity of nested floor powers - Paper B / K3 territory, parked behind BB/GG/JJ. Not a claim; recorded as the branch's target statement.
